title: Mini repair recipe compiler and safe-step packaging
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Build a lightweight compiler that converts existing prose-style incident repair instructions into small, idempotent 'repair recipes' composed of ordered, typed steps. Each compiled recipe must include a dry-run mode, permission checks, audit metadata and bounded side-effect primitives so on-call and support automation can execute, preview, or suggest remedial actions with minimal risk.
motivation: We have many ad-hoc runbooks and long procedural docs that are brittle to execute and hard to automate. Teams repeatedly rebuild one-off scripts for the same remediation patterns. By stepifying and packaging instructions as discrete, validated recipe artifacts we can reuse, test, and safely automate remediation while keeping human-in-the-loop review where required.
goals: Define a compact on-disk JSON/YAML recipe schema for stepified repairs
Build a command-line 'recipe-compiler' that ingests markdown runbook sections and emits validated recipes
Support 'dry-run' and 'simulate' modes that detect destructive steps and report expected changes without mutating systems
Expose a permission gating mechanism and per-step audit metadata so only authorized actors can run sensitive steps
Instrument telemetry for step success/failure, latency, and precondition checks
non_goals: Not a full replacement for complex orchestration engines (no distributed workflow persistence in phase 1)
No automatic root-cause detection or AI-driven remediation suggestions in phase 1
Not providing out-of-the-box cloud provider SDKs for every API (we'll provide a thin adapter interface)
design_summary: Recipes are immutable artifacts with a header (name, version, author, intent, tags), a sequence of typed steps (check, read, exec, shell, api-call, patch), and safety attributes (reversible, idempotent, required_approval). The compiler parses markdown blocks annotated with minimal inline metadata to generate step definitions. The runtime validates preconditions, enforces permission checks, and either simulates or executes each step within a constrained environment. A compact provenance record is emitted for every run and attached to the incident timeline.
acceptance_criteria: Recipe schema v1 documented in Confluence and validated by unit tests
CLI compiler can convert three canonical SRE markdown runbooks into recipes with >=90% fidelity
Recipe execution supports --dry-run mode and returns deterministic, human-readable diffs
Runtime produces a signed audit event for each step and stores provenance in the incidents service
Permission checks enforced: destructive steps require 'support:ops-run' role; otherwise execution halts with clear remediation guidance
implementation_plan: spec: finalize schema and step types (owner: Liam)
cli: recipe-compiler MVP that accepts markdown snippets and outputs recipe.json (owner: Priya)
runtime: add small execution harness to run validated steps in sandboxed containers with timeouts (owner: backend team)
auth: integrate with existing RBAC service to gate sensitive steps (owner: identity)
telemetry: emit step-level events to logging/metrics and wire to Console traces (owner: observability)
docs: how-to for converting runbooks and safe-execution checklist (owner: dev-docs)
rollout_plan: Alpha: Make feature available to SRE and Platform Support in a non-production sandbox; collect feedback
Canary: Enable recipe execution in a low-risk namespace with manual approval flow for destructive steps
Gradual rollout: unlock for on-call rotation groups after 2 weeks of successful canary runs
Post-rollout: offer conversion clinics to migrate top 20 high-value runbooks to recipe format
monitoring_and_telemetry: Emit events: recipe.run.start, recipe.step.start, recipe.step.end, recipe.run.end, recipe.run.error
SLOs: 99th percentile step execution latency target 2s for non-network-bound steps
Dashboards: step failure rate by recipe, top failing steps, recent dry-run diffs
Alerts: daily regression alert if newly converted recipes cause >5 failing runs in 24h
testing: unit: schema validation tests and step parser fuzzing
integration: run compiled recipes against a local simulated cluster and assert expected state transitions
chaos: intentionally fail preconditions to verify safe abort behavior
e2e: convert and run three example production runbooks as part of release smoke tests
